data.title: Corporate Access From Exposed Personal Devices
data.summary: Infostealer output and public exposure indicated corporate credentials and session material held on personal, unmanaged devices, placing corporate access outside every control the organisation operates.
data.description:
Work reaches personal devices through ordinary convenience: mail on a phone, a document opened at home, a password saved in a personal browser profile. The device is outside device management, has no EDR, and is shared.

Infostealer malware on such a device collects browser-stored passwords and, more importantly, session cookies — which authenticate without a password and therefore without multi-factor authentication. Those logs are sold in bulk, and corporate domains in them are easy to search for.

Because the compromise happens on a device the organisation cannot see, the first sign is usually a successful login that looks entirely normal.
data.recommendation:
* Provide a managed route for the work people do on personal devices, so the workaround is unnecessary.
* Use conditional access to require a managed, compliant device for anything sensitive.
* Monitor infostealer sources for your domains, and revoke sessions — not only passwords — on any hit.
* Keep session lifetimes short enough that a stolen cookie expires quickly.
data.short_recommendation: Separate corporate access from personal devices, and revoke sessions on exposure.
